title: How Some Skinny Guys Are Stronger Than Big Guys
tags: how to get strong at home
description:
Ever seen a skinny guy lift something he had no business lifting? It is not luck, and it is not fake. Some skinny guys are freakishly strong, and the reason is not the size of their muscles.

In 1988, Naim Süleymanoğlu, the weightlifter they called Pocket Hercules, weighed about 60 kg and lifted 190 kg over his head. That is more than three times his own body weight. This video breaks down the three hidden reasons behind that kind of strength: the physics of a light frame, the wiring of your nervous system, and your tendons, the steel cables that carry every bit of force your muscles make. Then you get a 12 week home plan to train them with no weights at all.

What you will learn:
• Why smaller bodies are stronger pound for pound (the square cube law)
• How your brain decides how much of your muscle you can actually use
• What tendon stiffness is and why stiff tendons make you faster and more explosive
• Why endless easy push ups build muscle but leave your tendons behind
• Why heavy loading changes tendons and light training barely does
• Why teenagers need to build tendon strength before ramping up training
• A 12 week isometric workout with just a towel, a wall and a pull up bar
• A simple dead hang test to track your progress
• The one food tip with early evidence for building collagen
